releases.name: v3.1.0
releases.body:
Welcome to Immich `v3.1.0`!

This release includes several quality of life improvements and another round of bug fixes. Keep reading below for the complete highlights.

## Highlights

- Upload wakelock (web)
- Undo archive (web)
- Filter assets by server filepath (workflows)
- Quick navigate to maintenance page (web)
- Better slideshow button accessibility (web)
- OIDC role claim sync improvements (OAuth)
- Invalidate sessions on password reset (admin-cli)

### Upload wakelock (web)

Similar to mobile, the web application will now automatically acquire a wakelock to prevent the screen from dimming while uploads are happening. This feature will require an HTTPS connection.

### Undo archive (web)

After archiving assets, the success notification now has an “undo” button to undo the action.

![Undo button on success notification](https://static.immich.cloud/blog/48ff8c50-260a-4114-a8a0-117d8989f622/48fe5c0071ecd3700696ea24516267dd.webp)

### Filter assets by server filepath (workflows)

The asset file filter has a new option “Use path”. When set to true, it will filter based on the actual path on the server rather than the original file name.

# v3.0.3

- various bug fixes
- we push to our own F-Droid repo at https://app.futo.org/fdroid/repo now. If you're using F-Droid, please pull the application from there from now on

> [!Note]

releases.name: v3.0.0
releases.body:
# v3.0.0

Welcome to Immich `v3.0.0`!

After months of hard work from the team and our amazing contributors, we're thrilled to announce the next major version of Immich: `v3.0.0`!  🎉 

## Breaking changes

This release includes several breaking changes; read the full migration guide [here](https://immich.app/blog/v3-migration). *It's worth mentioning that many of the breaking changes are updates to API endpoints and affect only **third-party tools** that integrate with Immich's API*. For the vast majority of users, updating works exactly as it always has.

## How to update

> [!WARNING]
> `v3.0.0` drops support for pgvecto.rs. If you run Immich before `v1.133.0` and haven't done the migration step yet, see the migration guide here. https://docs.immich.app/install/upgrading/#migrating-to-vectorchord

First, update the `IMMICH_VERSION` in your `.env` file to `v3`:

```diff
- IMMICH_VERSION=v2
+ IMMICH_VERSION=v3
```

Then run the usual update commands:

```bash
docker compose pull && docker compose up -d
```

aiSummary.oneLiner: A high-performance, self-hosted photo and video backup solution designed as a direct alternative to Google Photos.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Immich is a comprehensive self-hosted media gallery that provides seamless backup and organization for personal photos and videos. It features dedicated mobile applications for background synchronization and a responsive web interface for viewing and managing media. The backend is powered by Node.js and NestJS, utilizing machine learning for automatic facial recognition, object detection, and geographical clustering. It is designed to handle massive media libraries with high performance, offering users complete data sovereignty without sacrificing the modern features expected from cloud services.
keyFeatures: Automatic mobile backup: Syncs photos and videos in the background using native iOS and Android apps.
Machine learning integration: Automatically detects faces and objects for advanced search and clustering.
Multi-user support: Allows families to share a single instance while keeping individual libraries private.
High-performance media processing: Efficiently transcodes videos and generates thumbnails for fast loading.
Extensive localization: Supports dozens of languages for a global user base.
Data sovereignty: Keeps all personal media entirely on self-hosted infrastructure.

useCases.description: Migrating a family's entire media library away from paid cloud services to a local NAS.

useCases.title: Automated Archiving
useCases.description: Ensuring every photo taken on a mobile device is immediately and securely backed up home.

useCases.title: Media Organization
useCases.description: Using built-in facial recognition to easily find and group photos of specific family members.

useCases.title: Shared Galleries
useCases.description: Creating collaborative albums where multiple users can contribute media from different devices.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Privacy-conscious individuals and families who want a modern, feature-rich photo backup solution on their own hardware.
